title: Mutation Safety Envelope — Core Schema
description: Normative, domain-blind schema for MSE v0.2.0. This schema defines the safety envelope only. Domain-specific vocabulary (SKUs, fares, plans, billing periods, etc.) MUST NOT be added here — it belongs in a profile that extends `Effect.type` namespaces and `value` payloads. See /spec/normative-spec.md. v0.2.0 is a breaking revision of v0.1.0's mutation-wide CommitOutcome model, made in direct response to external falsification recorded in /docs/v0.2-review-response.md — see that document and /spec/normative-spec.md §9 before assuming v0.1.0 shapes still apply.

GuaranteeMode.description: Confidence classification for a predicted effect. EXACT: the value is guaranteed to hold at commit time if committed within validUntil. REVALIDATE: the value may drift and MUST be re-checked at or before commit. UNKNOWN: no guarantee is offered; the client MUST NOT rely on the value for acceptance-constraint evaluation.

validUntil.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Required when mode is EXACT or REVALIDATE if the guarantee is time-bounded. Absent validUntil with mode=EXACT means the guarantee does not expire before commit is attempted at all (implementations SHOULD still treat an unreasonably long-lived EXACT guarantee with suspicion; see security considerations).

effectId.description: Opaque, domain-blind identifier for this specific effect instance, unique within the MutationQuote it appears in (across all units — see /spec/normative-spec.md §7a). Added in v0.2.0: because multiple independently committing units may legitimately produce effects sharing the same `type` (e.g. two units each producing a `retail:order_total_delta`), `type` alone is no longer sufficient to correlate an effect across MutationQuote -> CommitResult -> Receipt. All quote/commit/receipt correlation MUST use `effectId`, not `type`. A provider MUST assign effectId at quote time and MUST NOT reuse an effectId for a different effect within the same quote.

type.description: Namespaced, domain-defined effect identifier in the form `<namespace>:<local_name>`, e.g. `retail:order_total_delta`. The MSE core assigns no meaning to any namespace or local_name; it only requires the shape. Profiles own the registry of meaningful values within their namespace. Not required to be unique within a quote — see effectId.

value.description: Domain-defined payload for this effect. The core treats this as opaque. Profiles SHOULD constrain `value` to a specific, documented shape per effect type (e.g. a signed decimal amount + ISO 4217 currency code for a *_delta effect), but the core schema intentionally does not.

proposalId.description: Client- or server-generated identifier for this proposal, unique within the issuing system. MUST NOT be reused across distinct proposals.

target.description: Opaque, domain-defined reference to the existing commercial resource being mutated (e.g. an order id, itinerary id, subscription id). The core does not interpret this value.

change.description: Opaque, domain-defined description of the proposed mutation. The core does not interpret this value; it is passed through to the provider that produces a MutationQuote.

CommittingUnit.description: Added in v0.2.0. A domain-blind representation of one independently committing unit within a MutationQuote. External review (UCP Discussion #799; see /docs/v0.2-review-response.md) established that a single mutation attempt may span several units that commit independently — e.g. one succeeds while another is refused or left indeterminate — and that v0.1.0's single mutation-wide CommitOutcome could not represent this without destroying information. The core assigns no domain meaning to what a unit is: it may correspond to a retail line, a travel leg, a subscription component, a contract clause, or anything else a profile/provider defines. The core only requires that the set of units be known no later than quote time, so a caller can check result coverage against a set it already saw before committing.

unitRef.description: Opaque, domain-blind, stable identifier for this committing unit, unique within the MutationQuote. A provider MUST NOT reuse a unitRef for a different unit within the same quote, and MUST use the same unitRef to refer to this unit in the corresponding CommitResult.unitResults entry.

effects.description: Predicted consequences of committing this specific unit. MAY be empty (a no-op or purely structural unit), but the array key MUST be present.

quoteId.description: Unique identifier for this quote. A commit request references this id.

target.description: Opaque reference to the resource this quote applies to. SHOULD match the `target` of the originating MutationProposal.

snapshot.description: Opaque, provider-defined precondition material representing the state of `target` at quote time (e.g. a version, ETag, content hash, or provider-internal token). The core assigns this value no shape or meaning and does not require it to be a universally comparable/updatable token — it is whatever the provider needs to detect drift by whatever mechanism the provider actually implements. A profile/adapter declaring `commitConsistency` other than NONE MUST document, in its own adapter documentation, what `snapshot` contains and how drift is actually detected (see /spec/normative-spec.md §6); the core does not and cannot verify this from the schema alone. Optional: not every provider can offer a snapshot reference.

units.description: Added in v0.2.0, replacing v0.1.0's top-level `effects` array. The complete set of independently committing units this quote proposes, known no later than quote time. A quote with only one unit is the degenerate (and still fully valid) single-unit case — v0.2.0 does not require multi-unit quotes, only that the shape can represent them. Every `unitRef` in this array MUST be unique within the quote (see /spec/normative-spec.md §1a); a quote with duplicate unitRefs is not conformant.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp after which this quote MUST NOT be committed. A commit attempted after expiresAt MUST be refused by a conformant provider. If absent, the quote does not expire independently of its effects' own guarantee.validUntil values (the commit consistency rules in the normative spec still apply).

commitConsistency.description: Declares how a provider will use `snapshot` at commit time. SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED: commit MUST be refused if the resource's current state does not match snapshot, by whatever provider-defined comparison the adapter documents. SNAPSHOT_ADVISORY: provider MAY warn or re-quote on drift but is not required to refuse. NONE: no snapshot-based drift detection is offered. The core does not require a universal/shared snapshot token scheme across providers, and does not require every mutation path into a resource to update the same tracked value — see /spec/normative-spec.md §6.

ComparableValue.description: A discriminated, domain-blind comparable value. This is a closed set of generic value SHAPES (number, money, timestamp, boolean, string) — not a set of domain concepts. Recognizing that a monetary amount carries a currency code is a primitive-typing concern, not a fare/SKU/plan/refund concept, and does not violate core domain-blindness (see /spec/normative-spec.md §4a). A profile's Effect.value MAY use this shape for any effect it wants to be constrainable via AcceptanceConstraint; the core assigns no domain meaning to which effectType uses which ComparableValue variant.

amount.description: Decimal amount encoded as a string (never a binary float) so implementations compare it with decimal-safe arithmetic instead of IEEE-754 floating point.

effectId.description: Changed in v0.2.0 (was `effectType`): the specific Effect.effectId this constraint applies to. Since multiple units may produce effects sharing the same `type`, a constraint naming only a `type` would be ambiguous about which unit's effect it bounds. A constraint MUST name one specific effect instance by its effectId.

value.description: Bound expressed as a ComparableValue. Comparison rules (normative, see spec §4a): a constraint MUST fail closed (be treated as violated) if the matching effect's value is not itself a ComparableValue of the identical variant `type` as this bound (e.g. a `money` bound against a `number`-typed effect value fails closed), and a `money` bound additionally MUST fail closed if `currency` does not match exactly. Money comparison MUST be performed with decimal-safe arithmetic over the `amount` string, never by parsing it into a native binary float.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque key supplied by the caller to allow safe retry of a commit request whose outcome is INDETERMINATE. MSE does not define the retry protocol itself (see 'What MSE does not define'); this field only reserves a place for one to be carried. As of v0.2.0, prefer per-unit UnitResult.reconciliation for actually resolving an INDETERMINATE unit — idempotencyKey remains useful as the correlation key a reconciliation path may reference, but reconciliation, not blind resubmission, is the normative resolution mechanism (see /spec/normative-spec.md §4a).

acceptanceConstraints.description: Bounds the caller requires to hold, checked against the final pre-commit quote. MAY be empty, meaning the caller accepts the quote unconditionally.

UnitOutcome.description: Renamed from CommitOutcome in v0.2.0 and now scoped to a single CommittingUnit rather than to the whole mutation attempt. See UnitResult and /spec/normative-spec.md §1a-§1c.

RefusalReason.description: A small standard vocabulary of core reasons, plus an open, namespaced extension mechanism for provider- or profile-specific reasons that do not fit the standard set. A conformant value is EITHER one of the five standard reasons below, OR a namespaced string in the form `<namespace>:<local_reason>` using the same namespacing convention as Effect.type (e.g. `travel:fare_class_closed`, `stripe:card_declined`). Providers SHOULD prefer a standard reason when one genuinely applies, and MUST use a namespaced extension rather than overloading PROVIDER_REJECTED when a more specific reason is available, so callers are not forced to lose information the provider actually has. See /spec/normative-spec.md §5.

ReconciliationMode.description: Added in v0.2.0. Classifies what kind of path, if any, exists to resolve an INDETERMINATE UnitResult. MACHINE_RESOLVABLE: a binding/profile-defined operation exists that a caller (or its agent) can invoke programmatically to learn the actual outcome — e.g. the reference implementation's reconciliation-by-idempotency-key. AUTHORITATIVE_READ: no dedicated reconciliation operation exists, but a binding can define an authoritative read/status path (e.g. re-fetching the target resource) whose result resolves the mutation's true outcome. NONE: no machine-resolvable path is available at all; the caller has no programmatic way to resolve the uncertainty and MUST fall back to non-MSE means (manual investigation, support escalation, etc.). A provider MUST NOT report MACHINE_RESOLVABLE or AUTHORITATIVE_READ unless a real path actually exists — pretending an unavailable recovery path is actionable is a conformance violation (see /spec/normative-spec.md §4b).

Reconciliation.description: Added in v0.2.0. Carried on an INDETERMINATE UnitResult. Provides enough structured information for a binding/profile to tell the caller what safe operation comes next, without MSE itself defining a transport or retry protocol (see /spec/normative-spec.md §4b for the full normative requirements a binding exposing MACHINE_RESOLVABLE or AUTHORITATIVE_READ must satisfy).

correlationId.description: Opaque key correlating a future reconciliation/read attempt back to this specific indeterminate attempt (and, transitively, to the unitRef it resolves — see /spec/normative-spec.md §4b). Required when mode is MACHINE_RESOLVABLE or AUTHORITATIVE_READ; MUST be absent when mode is NONE, since there is nothing to correlate a nonexistent path against.

reference.description: Opaque, binding-defined pointer describing how to actually invoke the reconciliation or authoritative-read path (e.g. an operation name, a resource locator, a polling descriptor). The core does not interpret this value; a binding exposing MACHINE_RESOLVABLE or AUTHORITATIVE_READ MUST document what it contains and how to use it. MAY be absent even when mode is not NONE, if the binding's documentation alone (rather than a per-response value) is sufficient to invoke the path.

UnitResult.description: Added in v0.2.0, replacing v0.1.0's mutation-wide outcome/refusalReason/committedEffects on CommitResult. One UnitResult per CommittingUnit in the originating quote — see /spec/normative-spec.md §1b for the complete-coverage requirement this implies.

unitRef.description: MUST match the unitRef of exactly one CommittingUnit in the quote referenced by this CommitResult.

refusalReason.description: Required when outcome is REFUSED for this unit.

committedEffects.description: Present when this unit's outcome is APPLIED. The effects as actually realized at commit time for this unit, which MAY differ from the quoted effects only for effects whose guarantee.mode was REVALIDATE or UNKNOWN. A conformant provider MUST NOT silently alter an EXACT-guaranteed effect between quote and commit; doing so is a conformance violation, not a valid APPLIED result (see spec). MUST be absent when outcome is REFUSED or INDETERMINATE for this unit — an INDETERMINATE unit in particular MUST NOT claim committedEffects, because the provider does not know whether they occurred (see /spec/normative-spec.md §6a).

reconciliation.description: Required when outcome is INDETERMINATE for this unit. MUST be absent otherwise.

AggregateHint.description: Added in v0.2.0. A non-authoritative, derived-only summary of CommitResult.unitResults, provided purely as a convenience for callers that want a fast path for the common single-unit or uniform-outcome case. THIS FIELD IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE. A caller MUST NOT treat aggregateHint as a substitute for inspecting unitResults, and MUST NOT collapse a MIXED result into any single APPLIED/REFUSED/INDETERMINATE decision. A conformant implementation computing this field MUST derive it purely from unitResults (ALL_APPLIED iff every unitResults[].outcome is APPLIED, ALL_REFUSED iff every one is REFUSED, ALL_INDETERMINATE iff every one is INDETERMINATE, MIXED otherwise) and MUST NOT allow it to disagree with unitResults.

unitResults.description: Changed in v0.2.0 (replaces the v0.1.0 mutation-wide `outcome`/`refusalReason`/`committedEffects` fields entirely — this is a breaking change, see /spec/normative-spec.md §9). MUST contain exactly one UnitResult per CommittingUnit present in the quote referenced by quoteId — a unit MUST NOT be silently omitted, and a UnitResult MUST NOT reference a unitRef absent from that quote. This is the complete-coverage requirement; see /spec/normative-spec.md §1b.

effectId.description: Changed in v0.2.0 (was `effectType`). Correlates this receipt entry to a specific Effect.effectId in committedEffects, not merely to a type — required because multiple units' committed effects may share the same `type` (see /spec/normative-spec.md §7a).

unitRef.description: Added in v0.2.0. The CommittingUnit this effect was committed under. Redundant with information derivable by cross-referencing effectId against the CommitResult, but included directly so a receipt is self-describing without requiring the reader to still hold the CommitResult.

value.description: Domain-defined realized value for this effect, when known. MAY be absent when finality is PENDING or UNKNOWN.

settledAt.description: Timestamp at which finality became FINAL or FAILED. Absent while PENDING or UNKNOWN.

effectReceipts.description: Changed in v0.2.0 (the v0.1.0 mutation-wide `mutationOutcome` field is removed from Receipt entirely — commit-unit determinacy is now fully carried by the corresponding CommitResult.unitResults, and must not be re-collapsed here; see /spec/normative-spec.md §6a). Fail-clear rule unchanged in spirit from v0.1.0, now scoped per unit: a provider MUST include exactly one EffectReceipt for every effect present in every APPLIED unit's committedEffects — an effect MUST NOT silently disappear from the receipt. An effect that is not independently trackable MUST still appear, with finality UNKNOWN, rather than being omitted. A REFUSED or INDETERMINATE unit contributes no entries here, since it has no committedEffects to report on (see /spec/normative-spec.md §6a).

description: This top-level schema is a container for the $defs above. MSE does not mandate a single wire envelope; implementations reference individual $defs (MutationProposal, MutationQuote, CommitRequest, CommitResult, Receipt) as needed for their transport.
